chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Gus Aikens, the trumpeter who lost his lip
summary: Danny gave Gus Aikens, from Jenkins Orphanage, his last job when he could not get his lip up.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You remember a great trumpet player named Gus Aikens used to work in one of them.

Yeah, I remember Gus Aikens. Well, Gus Aikens came out of Jenkins Orphanage with Jabbo. He was a good player. But he lost his lip. I gave him what I think was probably his last job, a little job I had on 110th Street. He came in and he couldn't get his lip up. But then he'd take a drink, and then nothing happened. Then he'd stand on the bandstand all night and apologize. The boss came up to me and said, 'He's a nice guy. He can't play?'
He was a good player at one time.
Oh yeah, he one of the tops, you know. And his brother, the trombone player...
